```{r m3-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`postrank` accepts five representations of a posterior distribution:
equal-weight posterior draws (`postrank_draws()`), exact finite distributions
(`as_postrank_draws()`), conditional normal posteriors
(`postrank_gaussian_coefficients()`), shared-state normal mixtures
(`postrank_mixture_coefficients()`), and externally computed pairwise
comparison probabilities (`postrank_probabilities()`). Within-criterion pairwise
comparison probabilities determine expected directional losses, whereas
composite targets, simultaneous cross-criterion events, marginal intervals, and
draw-based Monte Carlo diagnostics require richer posterior information (and in
`postrank()`, `objective = "minimax"`, `exact_G`, and `q` are exposed only for
`postrank_draws` inputs; see the summary table below).

For practical examples of building each input in R, see
[Preparing your posterior draws and comparison probabilities](a5-your-posterior-results.html).
Every calculation below runs directly in R or reads stored `postrank_example()`
objects without model fitting or an optimization solver.[^theory]

## Pairwise directional-error probabilities {#begin-with-one-criterion-and-one-reported-direction}

Let \(\theta_i\) be the target for entity \(i\), oriented so that larger values
mean higher reporting priority toward Grade 1. Conditioning on your observed
data and statistical model, define for every distinct pair \(i \ne j\):

\[
e_{ij} = \Pr(\theta_i \le \theta_j).
\]

Here \(e_{ij}\) is the posterior expected error cost of placing entity `i` ahead
of entity `j`. It is a pairwise comparison probability under the joint
posterior—not a difference between posterior means or a hypothesis-test
\(p\)-value. When exact equality has zero posterior probability
(\(\Pr(\theta_i = \theta_j) = 0\)), \(e_{ij} + e_{ji} = 1\); in general,
\(e_{ij} + e_{ji} = 1 + \Pr(\theta_i = \theta_j)\). Note that continuous
marginal distributions alone do not imply \(\Pr(\theta_i = \theta_j) = 0\) (for
example, if two entities were assigned the exact same random variable, they
would be equal with probability `1`).

`postrank` stores `NA` on the diagonal of `e` because an entity is never
compared against itself. All five standard input types in this article assume
zero probability of exact ties between distinct entities; posteriors with
positive tie probability use the separate functions described in
[Exact ties in the posterior versus withheld comparisons](m4-ties-and-withholding.html).

For any grading \(g\) with \(x_{ij}(g) = \mathbf{1}\{g_i < g_j\}\),
\(M = \binom{n}{2}\) unordered pairs, and \(N(g) = \sum_{i \ne j} x_{ij}(g)\)
ordered pairs, the single-criterion expected loss at withholding cost \(\tau\)
is

\[
R_\tau(g) = \frac{\sum_{i \ne j} x_{ij}(g) \, e_{ij} + \tau\{M - N(g)\}}{M}.
\]

By linearity of expectation, the matrix \((e_{ij})\) completely determines
\(R_\tau(g)\) without assuming that pairwise error indicators are independent;
see
[Posterior ranking, integer grades, and reporting loss](m1-ranking-and-loss.html).

## Why entity dependence matters {#marginal-distributions-can-leave-the-direction-unresolved}

Marginal posterior summaries for individual entities (means, standard errors,
or credible intervals) do not determine \(e_{ij}\) unless the joint dependence
across entities is also specified. Consider two three-state joint distributions
`Q1` and `Q2` for entities `A` and `B`, where each row has probability `1/3`:

```{r m3-couplings}
library(postrank)

couplings <- list(
  Q1 = cbind(A = c(0, 1, 2), B = c(1, 2, 0)),
  Q2 = cbind(A = c(0, 1, 2), B = c(2, 0, 1))
)
coupling_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(couplings), function(name) {
  z <- couplings[[name]]
  data.frame(
    law = name,
    states = paste(sprintf("(%s, %s)", z[, "A"], z[, "B"]), collapse = "; "),
    mean_A = mean(z[, "A"]), mean_B = mean(z[, "B"]),
    error_A_above_B = mean(z[, "A"] <= z[, "B"])
  )
}))
knitr::kable(coupling_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Law", "States (A, B)", "Mean A", "Mean B", "Error: A above B"))
```

Under both `Q1` and `Q2`, `A` and `B` have the exact same uniform marginal
distribution on \(\{0, 1, 2\}\) (mean `1`, variance `2/3`) and zero probability
of ties. Yet the posterior probability that placing `A` ahead of `B` is wrong
is `0.667` (`2/3`) under `Q1` and `0.333` (`1/3`) under `Q2`—reversing the
preferred direction! Sampling `A` and `B` independently from their marginals
would create a third distribution with positive tie probability (`1/3`).

When supplying posterior draws, keep all entities from the same posterior
iteration together in the same row `s`. Shuffling or sorting entity columns
independently preserves each entity's marginal histogram while destroying the
pairwise comparison probabilities.

## Exact finite laws versus Monte Carlo draws {#exact-states-and-monte-carlo-states-have-different-meanings}

`postrank` distinguishes two discrete state representations:

1. **Exact finite laws (`exact_finite_posterior` via `as_postrank_draws()`).**
   When a discrete posterior is defined completely by integer-valued states
   \(\theta^{(s)}\) and positive integer probability numerators sharing a common
   denominator (\(p_s\)),
   \[
   e_{ij} = \sum_s p_s \, \mathbf{1}\{\theta_i^{(s)} \le \theta_j^{(s)}\}
   \]
   is the exact mathematical probability. Building and aggregating an
   `exact_finite_posterior` input requires the suggested `gmp` package
   (`install.packages("gmp")`), which checks the exact integer masses and
   retains exact rational probabilities in `postrank_pairwise()` alongside the
   double-precision array `e` (exact rational coefficients still do not make
   downstream floating-point sums or MIP solves exact).
2. **Equal-weight posterior draws (`postrank_draws()`, `postrank_draws_from_array()`, `as_postrank_posterior()`).**
   Retained simulation draws approximate the underlying posterior by the sample
   average
   \[
   \widehat{e}_{ij} = \frac{1}{S} \sum_{s=1}^S
   \mathbf{1}\{\theta_i^{(s)} \le \theta_j^{(s)}\}.
   \]
   Even when \(\widehat{e}_{ij}\) equals `0` or `1` in a finite sample, the true
   posterior probability need not be `0` or `1`. Independent (`regime = "iid"`)
   and Markov chain Monte Carlo (`regime = "mcmc"`) draws use the same sample
   average \(\widehat{e}_{ij}\) but require different Monte Carlo uncertainty
   calculations, which is why `regime = "mcmc"` records chain IDs, iteration
   numbers, `warmup_per_chain`, and `thin`.

Standard draw constructors require full numerical precision without observed
within-criterion ties between entities (do not round exported draws or add
random jitter, which alters the posterior) and require equal weights `1 / S`
across retained draws (uneven importance weights are not accepted).

On `postrank_toy` (`32` independent draws for three entities on two criteria),
`postrank_pairwise()` aggregates `e[i, j, k]` in draw blocks without clipping
empirical `0` or `1` entries, and `postrank_evaluate()` evaluates any fixed
integer grading without running a solver:

```{r pairwise}
pairwise <- postrank_pairwise(postrank_toy, method = "blocks", block_size = 2L)
pairwise[["sample_sizes"]]
pairwise[["e"]][, , "need_A"]
weights <- c(need_A = 0.6, need_B = 0.4)
grade <- setNames(c(1L, 2L, 2L), postrank_toy[["entity_ids"]])
evaluation <- postrank_evaluate(grade, pairwise, weights, tau = 0.25)
evaluation[c("E_over_M", "E_over_N", "disclosure_rate", "weighted_risk")]
```

Placing `"001"` in Grade 1 and leaving `"site-B"` and `"site C"` together in
Grade 2 orders `N = 2` of the `M = 3` pairs. `E_over_M` divides expected
errors by `M`, and `E_over_N` divides by `N`. Supply positive integer grade
labels, with `names(grade)` matching `entity_ids` in the same order.
`canonical_postrank_grade()` renumbers occupied labels to `1, ..., G` while
preserving their pair relations.
Leaving all entities in Grade 1 (`N = 0`) sets `E_over_N` to `NA` and gives loss
`tau`—which is a withheld report, not an error-free ranking:

```{r all-abstain}
all_tie <- setNames(rep(1L, length(postrank_toy[["entity_ids"]])),
  postrank_toy[["entity_ids"]])
abstained <- postrank_evaluate(all_tie, pairwise, weights, tau = 0.25)
abstained[c("N", "E_over_N", "weighted_risk")]
```

## Conditional Gaussian and shared-state mixture posteriors

When entity posteriors are normal conditional on a fixed shared state \(h\)—with
conditional mean \(m_i(h)\), positive variance \(v_i(h) > 0\), and conditional
independence across entities given \(h\)—the pairwise directional-error
probability has the closed-form analytic expression

\[
e_{ij}(h) = \Phi\!\left(
  \frac{m_j(h) - m_i(h)}{\sqrt{v_i(h) + v_j(h)}}
\right),
\]

where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal cumulative distribution function.
For a jointly normal pair with conditional covariance \(c_{ij}(h)\), the
denominator is \(\sqrt{v_i(h) + v_j(h) - 2c_{ij}(h)}\) whenever the variance
of the difference is positive.
`postrank_gaussian_coefficients()` takes an `n x K` matrix of `means`, a
`K x K x n` array of within-entity `covariance` slices, and the explicit
declaration `conditional_independence = "entities_given_shared_h"`; cross-entity
covariance cannot be passed directly to this constructor.

Using the six-site normal distribution in `pr_tutorial`, we can compare
`postrank_gaussian_coefficients()` against both `pnorm()` and one-dimensional
numerical quadrature \(\int f_A(t)\{1 - F_B(t)\}\,dt\):

```{r m3-gaussian-build}
law <- pr_tutorial[["law"]]
gaussian <- postrank_gaussian_coefficients(
  means = law[["means"]][, "score_A", drop = FALSE],
  covariance = law[["covariance"]]["score_A", "score_A", , drop = FALSE],
  conditional_independence = "entities_given_shared_h",
  provenance = pr_tutorial[["one"]][["provenance"]]
)
```

```{r m3-gaussian-check}
mu <- law[["means"]][c("A", "B"), "score_A"]
sd <- sqrt(law[["covariance"]]["score_A", "score_A", c("A", "B")])
normal_formula <- pnorm((mu["B"] - mu["A"]) / sqrt(sum(sd^2)))
quadrature <- integrate(
  function(t) dnorm(t, mu["A"], sd["A"]) * pnorm(t, mu["B"], sd["B"], lower.tail = FALSE),
  lower = -Inf, upper = Inf, rel.tol = 1e-10
)
data.frame(
  calculation = c("Normal difference formula", "Numerical integral", "Package coefficients"),
  error_A_above_B = round(c(normal_formula, quadrature[["value"]],
    gaussian[["e"]]["A", "B", "score_A"]), 8)
)
```

All three calculations give `r sprintf("%.8f", normal_formula)` to eight decimal places.

The 30-site, three-criterion dataset `pr_example_gaussian` stores the exact same
known normal law from which the 4,000 independent draws in `pr_example_draws`
were simulated. We can check its supported capabilities and compare the
4,000-draw Monte Carlo probabilities against the analytic probabilities (each
indicator average has pointwise standard error at most \(\sqrt{0.25 / 4000}\),
distinct from a uniform weighted-loss envelope across all pairs):

```{r m3-gaussian-vs-draws}
caps <- postrank_coefficient_capabilities(pr_example_gaussian)
unlist(caps[c("weighted_expected_risk", "posterior_means",
  "minimax_problem", "target_state_trace")])
pw_4000 <- postrank_pairwise(pr_example_draws)
c(max_pointwise_diff = max(abs(pw_4000[["e"]] - pr_example_gaussian[["e"]]), na.rm = TRUE),
  five_se_band = 5 * sqrt(0.25 / 4000))
```

The stored normal analysis records how it obtained its report-card intervals
and whether it can estimate Monte Carlo error.

```{r m3-gaussian-diagnostics}
g <- postrank_example("gaussian_analysis_30x3")
g[["report_card"]][["interval_source"]]
gd <- postrank_coefficient_diagnose(pr_example_gaussian, fit = g[["fit"]])
gd[["diagnostics"]][["mcse_mean"]][["unavailable_reason"]]
gaussian_report <- postrank_report(g[["fit"]], diagnostics = gd,
  analysis = g, figures = FALSE)
gaussian_report[["diagnostic_table"]][, c("metric", "value", "available", "NA_reason")]
```

The report card records the interval source as
`r g[["report_card"]][["interval_source"]]` because it uses analytic normal
intervals. The draw-based `mcse_mean` is unavailable because this calculation
uses no hyperparameter chain.

### Shared-state mixtures {#a-shared-state-mixture-retains-the-shared-state}

In hierarchical normal or empirical-Bayes models where hyperparameters \(h_s\)
vary across quadrature nodes or MCMC draws with state probabilities \(\pi_s\),
marginal pairwise probabilities average the conditional normal probabilities
across states:

\[
e_{ij} = \sum_s \pi_s \, e_{ij}(h_s).
\]

`postrank_mixture_coefficients()` computes this average across shared states
`components` without simulating entity-level target draws:

```{r m3-mixture}
ids <- c("A", "B")
ks <- "k1"
cov_slice <- array(0.5, c(1L, 1L, 2L),
  dimnames = list(criterion_i = ks, criterion_j = ks, entity = ids))
make_state <- function(d) {
  list(
    mu = c(k1 = d),
    Sigma = matrix(1, 1L, 1L, dimnames = list(criterion_i = ks, criterion_j = ks)),
    means = matrix(c(d, 0.4), 2L, 1L, dimnames = list(entity = ids, criterion = ks)),
    covariance = cov_slice
  )
}
state_means <- c(s1 = -1, s2 = 0.5)
components <- lapply(state_means, make_state)
weights <- c(s1 = 0.5, s2 = 0.5)
state_index <- data.frame(state_id = names(state_means))
regime <- "fixed_finite_mixture"
independence <- "entities_given_shared_h"

# Hash the actual components, their generating recipe, and the mixture settings.
recipe <- list(formals = formals(make_state), body = body(make_state),
  state_means = state_means, covariance = cov_slice, entities = ids, criteria = ks)
config <- list(weights = weights, index = state_index,
  regime = regime, independence = independence)
mix_prov <- list(
  producer_id = "m3-vignette", producer_version = "1",
  posterior_id = "two-state-mixture",
  input_payload_sha256 = digest::digest(components, algo = "sha256"),
  source_sha256 = digest::digest(recipe, algo = "sha256"),
  config_sha256 = digest::digest(config, algo = "sha256")
)
mix <- postrank_mixture_coefficients(
  components, weights, state_index, regime, independence, mix_prov
)
round(mix[["e"]][, , "k1"], 4)
```

Because every entity is evaluated in the same state \(h_s\) before averaging
over \(s\), cross-entity dependence induced by shared hyperparameters is
preserved even though entities are conditionally independent given \(h_s\).
Replacing the mixture by a single normal distribution with overall means and
variances would change \(e_{ij}\). For report cards on mixture inputs, marginal
intervals are obtained by numerical inversion of the mixture cumulative
distribution function (if an endpoint fails probability verification after
rounding to target units, `posterior_quantile_failure` is recorded and the
validated grading is kept with the report card marked unavailable). For
`source_regime = "hyperparameter_mcmc"`, conditional-risk MCMC diagnostics
describe integration of expected risk across hyperstates rather than entity-draw
loss dispersion and require passing `chain_history` to
`postrank_coefficient_diagnose()`.

Note that the state probabilities `weights` (\(\pi_s\), summing to `1`) in
`postrank_mixture_coefficients()` are posterior mixture weights over states—not
criterion loss weights! Fixed mixtures (`source_regime = "fixed_finite_mixture"`)
accept general nonnegative state weights summing to `1`, whereas hyperparameter
MCMC states (`source_regime = "hyperparameter_mcmc"`) require uniform weights
`1 / length(components)` and a `state_index` recording `(state_id, chain_id, iteration)`.

## Joint draws versus separate criterion matrices {#several-criteria-need-jointness-for-some-questions}

With \(K\) criteria and nonnegative weights \(w_k\) summing to `1`, the
criterion-weighted loss replaces \(e_{ij}\) by
\(\bar{e}_{ij} = \sum_{k=1}^K w_k e_{ij,k}\). Because expectation is linear,
`postrank_draws()` accepts a named list of separate `S_k x n` criterion draw
matrices—potentially from separate models with different draw counts \(S_k\)—so
long as each matrix preserves the joint draws across entities for that
criterion. Row numbers from separate model fits do not link criteria into a
joint state.

To see what separate criterion matrices can and cannot support, fix entity `B`
at `(0, 0)` and compare two two-state distributions for entity `A` (each row has
probability `1/2`):

```{r m3-information-boundary}
criterion_laws <- list(
  Together = rbind(c(2, 2), c(-1, -1)),
  Opposite = rbind(c(2, -1), c(-1, 2))
)
information_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(criterion_laws), function(name) {
  a <- criterion_laws[[name]]
  data.frame(
    law = name,
    weighted_error = mean(rowMeans(a <= 0)),
    composite_error = mean(rowMeans(a) <= 0),
    both_criteria_correct = mean(rowSums(a > 0) == 2L)
  )
}))
knitr::kable(information_table, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Law", "Weighted error", "Composite error", "Both correct"))
```

For reporting `A` ahead of `B`, both distributions give equal-weight directional
error `0.5` and identical within-criterion probabilities (`0.5` on each
criterion). Yet the error on the composite `(theta_1 + theta_2) / 2` drops from
`0.5` under `Together` to `0` under `Opposite`, while the probability of being
right on both criteria drops from `0.5` to `0`.

Separate criterion matrices determine expected criterion-weighted loss and
per-criterion diagnostics, whereas draw-by-draw total-loss traces, `fragility`,
and `crossfit` in `postrank()` require joint `S x n x K` target draws; see
[Combining several criteria in one common grading](m2-several-criteria.html) and
[Monte Carlo diagnostics, cross-fitting, and IID bounds](m6-uncertainty-diagnostics.html).

## Externally computed comparison probabilities {#import-numerical-probabilities-with-their-calculation-limits}

`postrank_probabilities()` imports pairwise comparison probabilities calculated
outside `postrank`—for example, by numerical integration over a non-Gaussian
empirical-Bayes posterior (as in `pr_case_cde` and `pr_case_krw`):

```{r m3-direct-probabilities}
probabilities <- postrank_probabilities(
  gaussian[["e"]][, , "score_A"],
  criterion = "score_A",
  event = "directional_error", zero_ties = TRUE, margin = 0,
  source = list(
    kind = "analytic_reference",
    description = "Normal difference probabilities for pr_tutorial score A",
    conditioning = law[["conditioning"]]
  ),
  targets = c(score_A = "Illustrative standardized score; larger means higher priority")
)
identical(probabilities[["e"]], gaussian[["e"]])
```

Every call requires `event` (`"directional_error"` for \(\Pr(\theta_i \le \theta_j)\)
or `"higher_priority"` for \(\Pr(\theta_i > \theta_j)\); `$e` always stores
directional error), `zero_ties = TRUE`, `margin = 0`, `source`, and `targets`.
Diagonals must be `NA`, off-diagonals must lie in `[0, 1]`, and reverse pairs
must sum to `1` within `1e-12` under `correction = "none"` (the default).
Passing these local checks does not verify that a matrix comes from a coherent
joint posterior—for example, deterministic cycles (`A > B`, `B > C`, `C > A`
each with probability `1`) satisfy \(e_{ij} + e_{ji} = 1\) yet cannot arise from
scalar targets.

When quadrature or floating-point evaluation leaves small complement
discrepancies \(|P(i, j) + P(j, i) - 1| > 10^{-12}\), you can request
`correction = "symmetric"` with a finite `tolerance` in `[0, 1e-3]`. Both the
raw and symmetrized arrays are stored, along with the largest per-criterion
change \(d_k\). By the triangle inequality over the \(N(g)\) ordered pairs,
symmetrization changes the weighted loss of any fixed grading \(g\) by at most

\[
\frac{N(g)}{M} \sum_{k=1}^K w_k \, d_k.
\]

That bound measures only the adjustment from the supplied array to the
symmetrized array—not quadrature error or error relative to an unknown true
posterior.

## Exporting draws from an external MCMC workflow {#external-mcmc-producer-workflow}

In a hierarchical model—such as normal site-level targets with an
inverse-Wishart covariance prior fitted in Stan or JAGS—posterior sampling takes
place outside `postrank`. Export the post-warmup draws stacked chain by chain
and attach your study's descriptions. In the sketch below,
`my_identification_note` describes what identifies the site targets and
`my_tie_justification` explains why each between-site difference has zero
probability at zero under your model.

```{r producer-sketch, eval = FALSE}
# theta: 4000 x n x K array of post-warmup draws stacked chain by chain
# (rows 1:1000 chain 1, 1001:2000 chain 2, ...) from your Stan or JAGS fit.
decl <- postrank_declarations(
  targets = my_targets, context = my_context,
  provenance = my_provenance, origin = my_origin,
  identification_note = my_identification_note, tie_justification = my_tie_justification,
  joint_generation = "Each retained iteration holds all sites and criteria from one MCMC state.",
  sampling_provenance = "4 NUTS chains, 1000 warmup + 1000 post-warmup iterations each, thin = 1."
)
hb_draws <- postrank_draws(theta, regime = "mcmc", chains = 4L,
  warmup_per_chain = 1000L, thin = 1L, declarations = decl)
```

For a concrete `cmdstanr` layout, suppose your model file `normal_hb.stan`
defines one continuous normal site effect `theta[i]` per row of its input.
Supply the model data as `stan_data` and the site identifiers as `site_ids` in
that row order. The model here gives each between-site contrast a positive
conditional variance. Inspect sampler diagnostics, then extract the post-warmup
draws and match each Stan variable to its site.

```{r stan-repository-workflow, eval = FALSE}
fit_stan <- cmdstanr::cmdstan_model("normal_hb.stan")$sample(
  data = stan_data, chains = 4, iter_warmup = 1000, iter_sampling = 1000
)
fit_stan$cmdstan_diagnose()
site_variables <- sprintf("theta[%d]", seq_along(site_ids))
posterior_array <- fit_stan$draws(variables = "theta", inc_warmup = FALSE,
  format = "draws_array")
site_draws <- posterior_array[, , site_variables, drop = FALSE]
# R stores all iterations of chain 1 first, then all iterations of chain 2, etc.
theta <- array(as.numeric(site_draws),
  dim = c(dim(site_draws)[1] * dim(site_draws)[2], length(site_ids), 1L),
  dimnames = list(draw = NULL, entity = site_ids, criterion = "need"))
stan_decl <- postrank_describe(
  estimand = c(need = "Posterior site need parameter"),
  population = "Study sites", time = "2025-2026", units = "SD units",
  data = "Observed site outcome counts and covariates",
  model = "Hierarchical normal model in normal_hb.stan",
  identification = "Site random intercepts centered relative to grand mean",
  joint = "Each MCMC iteration jointly samples all sites",
  sampling = "4 NUTS chains x 1000 post-warmup draws stacked chain by chain, thin = 1",
  ties = "Each site contrast has a continuous conditional normal law with positive variance.",
  software = "CmdStan via cmdstanr", source = "normal_hb.stan fit",
  label = "hb-site-need", data_version = "2026-01", values = theta
)
stan_draws <- postrank_draws(theta, regime = "mcmc", chains = 4L,
  warmup_per_chain = 1000L, thin = 1L, declarations = stan_decl)
```

Exporting draws into `postrank` checks array shapes and metadata; it does not
establish MCMC convergence or model adequacy, and variational or point-estimate
approximations should not be labeled as `"mcmc"` draws.

## Summary of input representations and model scope

| Input constructor | Supported `postrank()` objectives | Extra summaries available | Not created by the constructor |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Joint draws (`postrank_draws()`, `S x n x K`) | `"weighted"` and `"minimax"`, `G_max`, `exact_G`, `q` | Report card, fragility, cross-fitting, diagnostics, IID bounds (`regime = "iid"`) | Proof of MCMC convergence or model adequacy |
| Separate criterion matrices (`postrank_draws(list(...))`) | `"weighted"` and `"minimax"`, `G_max`, `exact_G`, `q` | Report card, per-criterion diagnostics, IID bounds (when every criterion is `"iid"`) | Cross-criterion joint states, joint fragility/cross-fitting |
| Exact finite law (`as_postrank_draws()`) | `"weighted"` and `"minimax"`, `G_max`, `exact_G`, `q` | Exact rational `postrank_pairwise()` (requires `gmp`), report card | Validation of an external empirical posterior |
| Normal / mixture (`postrank_gaussian_coefficients()`, `postrank_mixture_coefficients()`) | `"weighted"` with `G_max` (`postrank_cuts()` also supports `exact_G`) | Report card, mixture state diagnostics (`postrank_coefficient_diagnose()`) | Entity target draws, empirical draw quantiles, general cross-entity covariance, fragility/cross-fitting |
| Supplied probabilities (`postrank_probabilities()`) | `"weighted"` with `G_max` (including `postrank_cuts()`) | Report card at stored `summaries$level` when `summaries` includes `lower`, `upper`, `level` | Posterior draws, joint events, intervals at other levels |

**Model fitting stays outside `postrank`.** `postrank` does not fit statistical
models; results depend on the posterior you supply. In a plug-in empirical-Bayes
analysis, any estimated prior held fixed when computing draws or probabilities
remains conditioned on unless hyperparameter uncertainty is propagated before
calling `postrank` (for example through `postrank_mixture_coefficients()` or
full hierarchical MCMC draws). Input validation checks array shapes, tolerances,
and required descriptions, not whether your statistical model is well specified
or calibrated.

[^theory]: JoonHo Lee (2026), *Decisions from Noisy Multidimensional Indicators:
